title: feature-flagged-telemetry-variance-experiments
content:
Purpose:
Run a set of controlled experiments driven by feature flags to reduce telemetry volume/cost and noise while preserving signal for SLOs and RCA. This doc captures experiment plans, metric defs, dashboard changes, and rollback criteria.

Context / motivation:
- Observability spend and dashboard query costs are growing faster than traffic.
- Many traces and high-cardinality metrics are rarely useful for post-mortem or alerting.
- We need a safe way to reduce volume (sampling, TTL, derivative metrics) without creating blind spots for latency regressions or model-quality issues.
- Feature flags let us rollout telemetry changes per-tenant or per-route and measure impact.

High-level experiment design:
1) Target telemetry knobs (feature-flag controlled):
   - trace_sampling_rate (range: 0.1% -> 100%)
   - span_prune_level (none | remove-kv-cache-spans | remove-session-metadata)
   - compact_trace_retention_days (1, 3, 7, 30)
   - metric_rollup_interval_s (1s -> 60s) for heavy counters
   - full_payload_collection (on/off) for a sample of requests

2) Cohorts / segmentation:
   - cohort A (control): current default telemetry config
   - cohort B (low sample): sample 1% traces, keep full spans for 7 days
   - cohort C (medium): sample 5% traces, prune session metadata, 3 day retention
   - cohort D (alias): tenant-level sparse telemetry (10% traces) + metric rollup 10s
   - cohort assignment: random by tenant-id hash, ensure min N tenants per cohort for power

3) Measurement windows:
   - short-term: 48 hours after stable rollout
   - primary analysis: 14 days
   - optional long-term: 90 day follow-up for drift/risk

Key metrics to track (metric definitions):
  - telemetry_cost_rate: USD/day for observability product (query + retention + storage).
  - trace_ingest_tps: traces per second ingested (count).
  - trace_size_bytes_p50/p95: median and tail of raw trace payload size.
  - essential_sli_alert_rate: alerts triggered by latency SLOs (count/day) -- important to detect missed alerts
  - latency_p50/p95_token_generation_ms: from token-gen span (ms).
  - session_reconstruct_success_rate: fraction of sessions we can stitch for RCA (95th percentile target >= 99%)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate: per-tenant KV cache hit ratio used for correlating latency spikes
  - investigation_time_median: median time from incident start -> first actionable trace link (hrs)

Operational thresholds / guardrails:
- If essential_sli_alert_rate deviates by >10% (relative) vs control for 2 consecutive days -> auto-rollback for that cohort.
- If session_reconstruct_success_rate drops below 97% -> pause rollout and escalate to SRE.
- If telemetry_cost_rate reduction < 2% after 14 days -> label experiment inconclusive and revert to avoid config drift.

Dashboard changes / exploration panels to build before rollout:
- Cohort comparison dashboard (side-by-side panels): trace_ingest_tps, trace_size_p95, telemetry_cost_rate, latency_p95, session_reconstruct_success_rate.
- Investigation-impact panel: list of incidents in window + whether full trace present (binary) + time to first trace.
- Sampling shadow test panel: show sample of traces that would have been dropped (store for 48h in cheap storage) and allow engineers to replay.
- Cost attribution panel: estimated cost delta per tenant per week (USD).

Trace sampling strategy details:
- Deterministic sampling by tenant-request-hash: ensures replayable and stable cohorts across retries.
- Implement two-phase sampling for critical prefixes: always keep traces tagged with e.g., "canary-rollout" or "e2e-test" with forced sample rate 100%.
- For multi-model fanout requests, sample all children if parent sampled; otherwise sample children at a reduced rate (0.5x parent sample rate) to preserve fanout visibility.

Session stitching considerations:
- Preserve minimal linking fields even when pruning spans: request_id, tenant_id, short-session_checksum.
- If span_prune_level removes session metadata, store a compact session index entry (tiny footprint) to allow coarse reconstruction for RCA.

Statistical plan / analysis notes:
- Primary outcome: change in telemetry_cost_rate and session_reconstruct_success_rate relative to control.
- Secondary outcomes: latency_p95, essential_sli_alert_rate, investigation_time_median.
- Minimum detectable effect: plan cohorts so we can detect a 5% change in session_reconstruct_success_rate with 80% power at alpha=0.05. Use historical baseline variance to compute N tenants needed.
- Use bootstrap on daily metrics for confidence intervals; avoid over-reliance on single-day p-values.

Rollout playbook (stepwise):
1) Dry-run: shadow sampling enabled for 48h (write-only to archived bucket). No actual pruning.
2) Canary: enable cohort B for 5 low-traffic tenants for 48h. Monitor dashboards + Slack alerts.
3) Ramp: expand to 20% traffic (stratified by region/model type) over 72h.
4) Full cohort assignment for experiment if no guardrail triggers at 14 days.
5) Evaluate and either fold changes into defaults or schedule iterative experiments.

Data retention and legal/compliance notes:
- Do not prune spans that contain PII tokens until KMS/HSM review. Feature flags that change payload retention must pass data-privacy checklist.
- For EU tenants, retention reductions must be approved by compliance if contract specifies retention windows.

Queries / SQL snippets (examples for analysis):
-- daily trace ingest by cohort
SELECT date_trunc('day', ingested_at) AS day, cohort, count(*) AS traces, approx_percentile(size_bytes, 0.95) AS size_p95
FROM observability.traces
WHERE ingested_at >= current_date - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1,2;

-- session reconstruction success by tenant
SELECT tenant_id, cohort, sum(reconstructed)/sum(total_sessions) AS recon_success
FROM observability.session_index
WHERE day BETWEEN '2024-12-01' AND '2024-12-14'
GROUP BY tenant_id, cohort;

Open questions / risks (to resolve before canary):
- Q: Are there tenant contracts that legally require full trace retention? (ACTION: legal review for top 10 enterprise tenants)
- Q: Do current trace schemas include small identifiers we rely on for RCA that will be removed by pruning? (ACTION: audit popular investigation playbooks)
- Risk: High-cardinality metric rollups may obfuscate per-route hotspots; ensure we keep raw counters for SLO-bound routes.
- Risk: Model-quality regressions that only appear in dropped traces (rare) — mitigate with targeted forced-sampling on retraining jobs.

Owner & stakeholders:
- experiment owner: Diego Alvarez (obs eng)
- SRE contact: Asha Menon
- Product / CS notified: Rebecca Chen (product-observability), ops-responders

Checklist before canary:
- [ ] Feature-flag gates implemented in runtime and control plane
- [ ] Cohort assignment deterministic and exposed in tenant metadata
- [ ] Cohort dashboards created and accessible to oncall (links added to incident runbook)
- [ ] Archived shadow bucket + replay tooling validated
- [ ] Legal/compliance review for retention changes completed
- [ ] Pager and escalation playbook updated for experiment cohorts

Notes-to-self / heuristics learned from prior experiments:
- Always keep a tiny breadcrumb span for every request: request_id + timestamp (adds ~40 bytes) and enables investigation even with aggressive pruning.
- Rolling back telemetry changes is non-invasive but often requires config sync across services; automation is key.
- Visual diff dashboards (control vs cohort) are the fastest way to spot regressions for SRE rotation.

Next steps:
- Finalize power calculation and publish required sample size (by tenant count).
- File ENG-1742 PR for control-plane changes and link to this doc.
- Schedule a 30m sync with SRE/Product next week to validate thresholds and legal items.

References and inspiration:

- external: OTel sampling recommendations, Honeycomb sampling case studies

End of doc.
